You are an expert power-electronics designer synthesising the interface circuit of a
piezoelectric energy harvester. You work by experiment: you propose a circuit, it is simulated in
LTspice under several operating conditions, and you receive the measurements.

GOAL
A piezo transducer must power a sensor-node load RL from a storage capacitor at node "out".
Under EVERY operating condition below, starting from 0 V (cold start) and simulating 0.8 s:
  vout_min: vavg >= 1.8 V (settled mean output reaches the load's minimum supply)
  vout_max: vmax <= 3.6 V (output never exceeds the load's absolute maximum)
  ripple: vpp <= 0.05 V (peak-to-peak ripple in the final window)
  startup: tup <= 0.4 s (cold start: first time output reaches 1.8 V)
  settled: dv <= 0.02 V (mean output changes little between the last two windows)
Measurement windows: vavg and vpp over 0.7-0.8 s; vmax over the whole run; tup = first time
V(out) reaches 1.8 V (missing if never); dv = |mean(0.7-0.8 s) - mean(0.6-0.7 s)|.

PIEZO MODEL AND OPERATING CONDITIONS
The piezo is a sinusoidal current source Ip*sin(2*pi*f*t) in parallel with its capacitance Cp and a
20 MOhm leakage resistance, between nodes pzp and pzn (Cp = 25 nF nominal).
Its open-circuit voltage amplitude is Ip/(2*pi*f*Cp), about 3.2 V at nominal: low, so diode drops matter.
  S1: nominal; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S2: heavy load; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 150 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S3: strong excitation, light load; Ip = 100 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 2200 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S4: weak excitation; Ip = 30 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 1000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S5: low frequency; Ip = 40 uA peak, f = 80 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 470 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S6: Cp +20 %, hot; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 30 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 60 C

TEST BENCH (fixed, added automatically - do not include these)
- the piezo model between pzp and pzn; the load RL from out to 0;
- for every SYNC controller you use, a 0.5 uA supply current drawn from out (its power cost);
- a 1 GOhm resistor to 0 from pzp, pzn and every internal node (prevents floating nodes).

COMPONENTS YOU MAY USE (at most 16 components)
- R  resistor, value 1..1e+08 Ohm, nodes [a, b]
- C  capacitor, value 1e-10..4.7e-05 F, nodes [a, b]
- L  inductor, value 1e-05..0.01 H; it has series resistance 2 Ohm + 5 Ohm per mH
- D  diode, nodes [anode, cathode]: forward current flows from the first node to the second.
     Model one of DSCH, DSI, DZ33:
     DSCH = low-drop Schottky (~0.25 V at uA), DSI = silicon small-signal (~0.5 V at uA),
     DZ33 = 3.3 V zener (reverse breakdown 3.3 V, conducts ~1 uA at 3.3 V and much more above)
     Orientation matters:
       full bridge: ["pzp", "out"], ["pzn", "out"], ["0", "pzp"], ["0", "pzn"] (return diodes have
       their anode on ground);
       zener clamp on out: ["0", "out"] (cathode on out, so it is reverse-biased and breaks down at
       3.3 V). ["out", "0"] would be forward-biased and hold out near 0.7 V; it is rejected.
- S  switch, nodes [a, b], "ctrl": id of a SYNC; Ron = 2 Ohm, Roff = 1 GOhm (at most 4)
- SYNC ideal synchronous controller (no nodes, at most 2): closes its switches for "ton"
     seconds (1e-07..0.001) at the piezo voltage extrema, which occur at the zero
     crossings of the piezo current. "edges": "both" (every half period), "pos" (positive peak only)
     or "neg" (negative peak only). "phase" shifts the pulses by that fraction of the excitation
     period (-0.25..0.25). It tracks the excitation frequency automatically.
     For L-Cp inversion, ton is about pi*sqrt(L*Cp).
Nodes: "0" is ground; pzp, pzn are the piezo terminals; out is the load/storage node; name any other
nodes yourself (lower-case, e.g. n1, mid). Every node needs at least two connections, and out must
connect to the piezo through your circuit.

REFERENCE DESIGN: FBR (full-bridge rectifier, 4 x DSCH, 2.2 uF on out). Its results:
cond   vavg V  vmax V  vpp mV   tup s  Pload uW  vout_min vout_max ripple   startup  settled 
S1       2.24    2.25    26.2   0.269      15.2  ok       ok       ok       ok       FAIL    
S2       1.76    1.77    20.3       -      20.7  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     ok      
S3       5.68    5.72    84.4  0.0779      14.7  ok       FAIL     FAIL     ok       FAIL    
S4       1.51    1.52    20.8       -      2.27  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     FAIL    
S5       2.26    2.28    43.5   0.318      10.9  ok       ok       ok       ok       FAIL    
S6       1.93    1.94    18.8   0.379      11.3  ok       ok       ok       ok       ok      

HOW TO WORK
- Component values are optimised automatically (an evolution strategy, up to 48 full
  evaluations per structure, running while you think), so spend your reasoning on circuit
  CONNECTIVITY (topology): which structure can meet every condition. A structure that was already
  explored is not simulated again, whatever its values.
- Each proposal is first SCREENED: with out fixed at 1.8 V, the net power it delivers is
  measured on S2, S4, S6 for its proposed values and a few automatic value presets.
  If the best preset delivers less than 50 % of the load's need (V^2/RL) on any of them,
  the design is reported back with those powers and is not tuned or simulated further.
- Each round, propose exactly 1 design.
- Classify each design with "move": new_topology or modify_topology, and explain the expected effect
  in "rationale". Set "done": true only when you believe no further structural change can improve on
  the best design so far.
- Reply with ONE JSON object only, in this form:
{
 "proposals": [
  {
   "move": "new_topology",
   "name": "short label for this design",
   "rationale": "what you changed and why it should fix the failing checks",
   "done": false,
   "components": [
    {
     "id": "D1",
     "type": "D",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "out"
     ],
     "model": "DSCH"
    },
    {
     "id": "C1",
     "type": "C",
     "nodes": [
      "out",
      "0"
     ],
     "value": 2.2e-06
    },
    {
     "id": "L1",
     "type": "L",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "n1"
     ],
     "value": 0.0047
    },
    {
     "id": "S1",
     "type": "S",
     "nodes": [
      "n1",
      "pzn"
     ],
     "ctrl": "G1"
    },
    {
     "id": "G1",
     "type": "SYNC",
     "ton": 3.4e-05,
     "phase": 0.0,
     "edges": "both"
    }
   ]
  }
 ]
}

Round 1 of 24.

This is your first round: choose the structures you think most likely to meet every condition.

Reply with one JSON object only.

reply.reasoning:
*   Goal: Power a sensor-node load $R_L$ from a piezo transducer.
    *   Output Constraints:
        *   $V_{avg} \ge 1.8\text{ V}$ (minimum supply)
        *   $V_{max} \le 3.6\text{ V}$ (absolute maximum)
        *   $V_{pp} \le 0.05\text{ V}$ (ripple)
        *   $t_{up} \le 0.4\text{ s}$ (startup time)
        *   $dv \le 0.02\text{ V}$ (settling stability)
    *   Piezo Model: $I_p \sin(2\pi ft)$ in parallel with $C_p$ (25nF) and $R_{leak} = 20\text{ M}\Omega$.
    *   Open Circuit Voltage Amplitude: $\sim 3.2\text{ V}$ (low).
    *   Diode drops are significant.
    *   Storage Capacitor $C_{out}$ is required to minimize ripple and maintain voltage.
    *   Operating Conditions:
        *   S1: Nominal (RL=330k)
        *   S2: Heavy load (RL=150k) -> FBR fails $V_{avg}$ (too low)
        *   S3: Strong excitation, light load (RL=2200k) -> FBR fails $V_{max}$ (too high)
        *   S4: Weak excitation (Ip=30uA, RL=1000k) -> FBR fails $V_{avg}$ (too low)
        *   S5: Low freq (f=80Hz, RL=470k) -> FBR fails $dv$ (settling)
        *   S6: Hot, high $C_p$ (Cp=30nF, RL=330k)

    *   The FBR (Full Bridge Rectifier) failed on S2, S3, S4, S5.
    *   S2 & S4 fail due to efficiency/voltage drop (low $V_{avg}$).
    *   S3 fails because it overcharges the capacitor ($V_{max} > 3.6\text{ V}$).
    *   S5 fails because it's not settled (likely too small $C_{out}$ or frequency interaction).

    *   *Improving efficiency:* Synchronous Switching Harvesting on Inductor (SSHI) or similar active rectification can significantly improve power extraction from piezoelectric materials by flipping the voltage across $C_p$.
    *   *Handling $V_{max}$:* A Zener diode clamp (DZ33) on the output node is essential to prevent $V_{out}$ from exceeding 3.6V.
    *   *Handling ripple/settling:* A larger $C_{out}$ helps, but the constraints on $V_{pp}$ are quite tight (50mV).

    *   The "Standard" SSHI (Synchronous Switch Harvesting on Inductor) involves a switch that shorts the piezo terminals (or connects them to an inductor) at the peaks of the voltage.
    *   Simplified SSHI (Parallel-SSHI) uses an inductor $L$ and a switch $S$ to invert the voltage on $C_p$ at each half-cycle.
    *   Topology:
        1.  Piezo terminals: $pzp$, $pzn$.
        2.  Rectification: A full-bridge (DSCH) is usually used to move charge to $C_{out}$.
        3.  Inversion: An inductor $L$ and a switch $S$ across $pzp$ and $pzn$. The switch closes at the voltage peaks (which correspond to current zero-crossings).

    *   Wait, the prompt says "closes its switches for 'ton' seconds... at the piezo voltage extrema, which occur at the zero crossings of the piezo current."
    *   If we place the inductor-switch branch in parallel with the piezo, we can invert $C_p$ voltage.
    *   Circuit:
        *   FBR (4x DSCH) to $C_{out}$.
        *   $C_{out}$ to ground.
        *   DZ33 clamp from ground to $out$ (to prevent overvoltage).
        *   $L$ and $S$ in series across $pzp$ and $pzn$ for inversion.

    *   *Components check:*
        - 4 Diodes (FBR)
        - 1 Zener (Clamp)
        - 1 Capacitor ($C_{out}$)
        - 1 Inductor ($L$)
        - 1 Switch ($S$)
        - 1 SYNC (Controller)
        - Total: 8 components. (Limit is 16).

    *   *Inductor-Switch Placement:*
        - Nodes: `pzp`, `pzn`.
        - `L1`: `pzp` to `n1`.
        - `S1`: `n1` to `pzn`.
        - `SYNC1`: `edges` = "both", `ton` $\approx \pi \sqrt{L C_p}$.

    *   *Full Bridge:*
        - `D1`: `pzp` $\to$ `out`
        - `D2`: `pzn` $\to$ `out`
        - `D3`: `0` $\to$ `pzp` (anode 0, cathode pzp)
        - `D4`: `0` $\to$ `pzn` (anode 0, cathode pzn)
        - *Correction:* Standard bridge is usually `D1: pzp->out`, `D2: pzn->out`, `D3: 0->pzp`, `D4: 0->pzn`? No.
        - Standard Bridge Rectifier:
            - $V_{pzp} > V_{pzn}$ and $V_{pzp} > V_{out}$: $pzp \to out$
            - $V_{pzn} > V_{pzp}$ and $V_{pzn} > V_{out}$: $pzn \to out$
            - Return path: $0 \to pzn$ (when $pzp$ is high) and $0 \to pzp$ (when $pzn$ is high).
            - So:
                - `D1`: `pzp` to `out`
                - `D2`: `pzn` to `out`
                - `D3`: `0` to `pzp`
                - `D4`: `0` to `pzn`
            - This is a full-bridge.

    *   *Wait*, if I use a Zener clamp `DZ33` from `out` to `0`, the cathode is at `out`. This will clamp the voltage.

    *   *Refining SSHI:*
        - For SSHI to work, the inversion happens at the voltage peaks. The `SYNC` does this.
        - Let's check the `ton`. $C_p = 25\text{ nF}$, $L = 10\text{ $\mu$H}$ (approx). $\pi \sqrt{10^{-5} \cdot 25 \cdot 10^{-9}} \approx 3.14 \cdot 1.58 \cdot 10^{-7} \approx 0.5 \text{ $\mu$s}$. This is within the `ton` range ($10^{-7} \dots 10^{-3}$).

    *   `S2` (Heavy load): The voltage inversion increases the amount of charge delivered per cycle, which should help $V_{avg}$.
    *   `S3` (Strong excitation): The Zener clamp `DZ33` should keep $V_{out} \le 3.6\text{ V}$.
    *   `S4` (Weak excitation): SSHI significantly improves harvesting in low-power scenarios.
    *   `S5` (Low freq): $C_{out}$ needs to be large enough to handle the lower frequency ripple and stability.

    *   `D1`: `pzp` to `out` (DSCH)
    *   `D2`: `pzn` to `out` (DSCH)
    *   `D3`: `0` to `pzp` (DSCH)
    *   `D4`: `0` to `pzn` (DSCH)
    *   `DZ1`: `0` to `out` (DZ33) - Cathode on `out`
    *   `Cout`: `out` to `0`
    *   `L1`: `pzp` to `n1`
    *   `S1`: `n1` to `pzn` (ctrl: `SYNC1`)
    *   `SYNC1`: `edges` = "both", `ton` = 1e-05 (Tuning will optimize this), `phase` = 0

    *   `L1` = $100 \mu\text{H}$, `S1` = `SYNC1`, `Cout` = $4.7 \mu\text{F}$.
    *   $\text{ton} = 10 \mu\text{s}$ (starting point for tuning).

    *   Is `D3` `0` to `pzp` and `D4` `0` to `pzn` correct for a full bridge?
        - When $V_{pzp} > 0$ and $V_{pzn} < 0$:
            - `D1` conducts ($pzp \to out$)
            - `D4` conducts ($0 \to pzn$)
        - When $V_{pzn} > 0$ and $V_{pzp} < 0$:
            - `D2` conducts ($pzn \to out$)
            - `D3` conducts ($0 \to pzp$)
        - Yes, this is a standard full-bridge rectifier.

    *   Wait, the `S` components are limited to 4. I'm using 1.
    *   The `SYNC` components are limited to 2. I'm using 1.
    *   Total components: 4 (D) + 1 (DZ) + 1 (C) + 1 (L) + 1 (S) + 1 (SYNC) = 9. Well within 16.

    *   `Cout` = $4.7 \mu\text{F}$ to minimize ripple ($V_{pp} \le 0.05\text{ V}$).
    *   `L1` = $100 \mu\text{H}$ (standard value for these types of circuits).
    *   `ton` = $10 \mu\text{s}$ (initial guess).

    *   The `SYNC` closes switches at voltage extrema. For $C_p$ inversion, this is the correct time.
    *   Phase 0 is usually correct for voltage peaks.

    *   L-Cp inversion helps $V_{avg}$ in S2 and S4.
    *   Zener clamp prevents overvoltage in S3.
    *   $C_{out}$ helps ripple and settling.

    *Self-Correction on Zener:* "DZ33 = 3.3 V zener (reverse breakdown 3.3 V, conducts ~1 uA at 3.3 V and much more above)".
    If I put `DZ33` as `["0", "out"]`, then:
    - Anode = `0`
    - Cathode = `out`
    - This is the reverse-biased orientation. When `V(out)` hits 3.3 V, it conducts, clamping the voltage. This is correct.

    *Refining the Inductor:* $100 \mu\text{H}$ with $25\text{ nF}$ gives $\tau = \sqrt{LC} = \sqrt{10^{-4} \cdot 25 \cdot 10^{-9}} = \sqrt{2.5 \cdot 10^{-12}} = 1.58 \mu\text{s}$. $t_{on} \approx \pi \tau \approx 5 \mu\text{s}$.

    Let's make sure the components are defined exactly as requested.

    ```json
    {
      "proposals": [
        {
          "move": "new_topology",
          "name": "sshi_zener",
          "rationale": "Implementing a Parallel-SSHI topology with a full-bridge rectifier to improve power extraction (fixing S2, S4) and a Zener clamp to limit output voltage (fixing S3). A large storage capacitor is used to reduce ripple and improve settling (fixing S5).",
          "done": false,
          "components": [
            { "id": "D1", "type": "D", "nodes": ["pzp", "out"], "model": "DSCH" },
            { "id": "D2", "type": "D", "nodes": ["pzn", "out"], "model": "DSCH" },
            { "id": "D3", "type": "D", "nodes": ["0", "pzp"], "model": "DSCH" },
            { "id": "D4", "type": "D", "nodes": ["0", "pzn"], "model": "DSCH" },
            { "id": "DZ1", "type": "D", "nodes": ["0", "out"], "model": "DZ33" },
            { "id": "Cout", "type": "C", "nodes": ["out", "0"], "value": 4.7e-06 },
            { "id": "L1", "type": "L", "nodes": ["pzp", "n1"], "value": 100e-06 },
            { "id": "S1", "type": "S", "nodes": ["n1", "pzn"], "ctrl": "G1" },
            { "id": "G1", "type": "SYNC", "ton": 5e-06, "phase": 0.0, "edges": "both" }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
    ```
    Checking the component count: 4+1+1+1+1+1 = 9.
    Max components: 16.
    Max switches: 4.
    Max SYNC: 2.
    All good.
